newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil can't cut scorned B Band area price for now.
newsitem.headline: Brazil can't cut scorned B Band area price for now.

text.p: The Brazilian government cannot lower the asking price for the only B Band cellular concession area that did not draw any bids for at least 40 days, the government said.

Investors want a reduction in the base price for the No. 8 B Band area, the only one that did not arouse any interest. But that will have to wait until the auctions for the other nine regions are completed.
"By law, nothing can be done until after the present tender process is closed, until after all the documentation is submitted and bids are opened and known," a Communications Ministry spokesman said.
"That won't happen for another 40 to 45 days," he said.
He confirmed news reports that consortia that submitted offers Monday on nine of 10 B Band concession areas offered by the government have asked Brasilia to lower the base price of area No. 8.

The government had set a minimum price of $200 million for the area, comprising the remote and sparsely populated northern states of Amazonas, Amapa, Maranhao, Para and Roraima. But investors say the price has to come down to draw bids.
The spokesman described rumors the government may reduce the base price as "mere speculation."
"Only after the tender process is closed can the price be changed or the bid specifications altered," he added.
The government expects to rake in a total of at least $5 billion for licensing fees for all 10 B Band areas, with Sao Paulo city and other metropolitan areas drawing the highest bids.
